subject: Fwd: PLANNING GROUP: What we have done so far on wildfire
body:
---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Ron Nehring, Crest Planning Group Chairman <
ronnehring@ronnehring.ccsend.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 27, 2025 at 3:26 PM
Subject: PLANNING GROUP: What we have done so far on wildfire
To: <associationofplanninggroups@gmail.com>

Fellow Planning Group Chairs,

Following the interest and feedback I received regarding our new Firewise
USA site, I wanted to share additional resources and insights from our work
on wildfire preparedness and evacuation in our subregion. I’m also
interested in knowing what work your Planning Group has done that perhaps
we have not thought of so we can strengthen our efforts.

In 2021, our Planning Group established a dedicated working group on
wildfire and evacuation. Over the course of three years, we held meetings
and engaged extensively with stakeholders—including our local fire
district, Cal Fire, the Crest Fire Safe Council, representatives from the
County, the Sheriff’s Department, and others—to identify the most effective
ways to reduce wildfire risk and enhance evacuation capacity.

This effort culminated in a comprehensive package of seven wildfire-related
resolutions, which our Planning Group unanimously adopted in the summer of
2024. Given our advisory role to the County of San Diego, each resolution
is framed as a recommendation to County. You can review the full package of
resolutions, along with a summary, here: Crest Planning Group Fire
Resolutions.
<https://qkdpmrbab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mFkEHQNHUD9eD9iISPIns5FG_ULzYDKfwL370ekp8zFRSuJLdhQlJVShatP__5WDqsOxEzOSLt0N1DkC0uglT12fnpaypLueU2s1G3PpLX2QIxvykqsJlEMDcC2miEM8Bqv622WJ-69pcxx7i8NhOTmgjqk0B0mJfPKWnaIxBjT80ovcsz0UKyYqnOwPhYVdrhyFb7VvbHFgfL3SukQfI6qrOJzATK-R_tAmMvo4ITcM4-w9Z2LD4LLQyr3L6ijIc_JBgR4xPXZ5jMCN4IXalwne9xF64Dap01AmRYnkT7NxXK9j5oEi_w==&c=ERxGsiFKnZq_gvENtQyYH_VGC_BObKJP-ELMYVlz7d14eovZEICI3g==&ch=rD2dwtFjPizs53SXvEbAcFQ4gOqZskG8cphp18ludxHrcNs_jLzgRg==>

One key takeaway from our work was the value of the Firewise USA program
<https://qkdpmrbab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mFkEHQNHUD9eD9iISPIns5FG_ULzYDKfwL370ekp8zFRSuJLdhQlJbhWf01s1ydyDxoyackA2RcQNTEfRlDPkbHmX2MuO8PBPswQ8KgE-rcyjYWxx1MCWnw0BK9QNwVPRmMPe--vv-_HOnhwjgONujomYHLomm1G-istWt-z54Z9ytb_uSjY54cNszAN2-4h6nrYtrH8BE9W20iK5zGCgg==&c=ERxGsiFKnZq_gvENtQyYH_VGC_BObKJP-ELMYVlz7d14eovZEICI3g==&ch=rD2dwtFjPizs53SXvEbAcFQ4gOqZskG8cphp18ludxHrcNs_jLzgRg==>,
which allows groups of at least eight homeowners to establish a Firewise
USA site, take steps to reduce wildfire risk, and potentially qualify for
homeowners insurance discounts.

Recognizing its benefits, one of our seven resolutions specifically
encourages and supports the formation of Firewise USA sites throughout our
subregion.

After I became Chairman of our Planning Group, we launched a website to
better serve our residents by providing access to essential information.
While the County’s webpage for our Planning Group exists, it is difficult
to find and lacks comprehensive resources. Our goal was to create a one-stop
hub where residents can find details about our Planning Group’s work,
wildfire preparedness, code enforcement, defensible space requirements, and
more. You can visit the site at: CrestPlanningGroup.com
<https://qkdpmrbab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mFkEHQNHUD9eD9iISPIns5FG_ULzYDKfwL370ekp8zFRSuJLdhQlJbhWf01s1ydyNiKG57PrvAcVhxPjLGUulw37A996ASKMyLn1vsnrei-gZWKYuy2livonBtHIF9k9VG_wnP-b7EVEi0hg9ftQc50vEBE2M1Z12ueCdNq6VOI=&c=ERxGsiFKnZq_gvENtQyYH_VGC_BObKJP-ELMYVlz7d14eovZEICI3g==&ch=rD2dwtFjPizs53SXvEbAcFQ4gOqZskG8cphp18ludxHrcNs_jLzgRg==>
.

At our next Planning Group meeting on Monday, February 10 at 6:30 PM at the
Crest Community Association Clubhouse, 113 North Park Drive, El Cajon we
will discuss the Firewise USA program and how to establish additional sites
in our subregion. I invite you to join us for this discussion—if you or
members of your Planning Group plan to attend, please let me know in
advance so I can ensure you are introduced. Google maps
<https://qkdpmrbab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001mFkEHQNHUD9eD9iISPIns5FG_ULzYDKfwL370ekp8zFRSuJLdhQlJbhWf01s1ydykexf6WkHNMJC4WTlUCRh3jzKPtSIxU6PCR-kc7cGljF6zwy53RYBlN1oKlhju9Q-BW6Qd2q3qIReUPxhXLessZ-z2CIaStIq64BZ0WyPags=&c=ERxGsiFKnZq_gvENtQyYH_VGC_BObKJP-ELMYVlz7d14eovZEICI3g==&ch=rD2dwtFjPizs53SXvEbAcFQ4gOqZskG8cphp18ludxHrcNs_jLzgRg==>

We have made progress but we have a very long way to go before the wildfire
threat in our subregion has been materially reduced. To this end,
Resolution 1 in our package established wildfire threat reduction as the
top priority for our Planning Group.

I think sharing ideas and best practices at, and in between, our APG
meetings can help us all in our efforts to improve our communities and make
them safer. I hope you find this information useful, and look forward to
hearing about the work you've done.

All the best,
[image: Ron Nehring]

Ron Nehring

Chairman, Crest-Dehesa-Granite Hills-Harbison Canyon Planning Group

Here is  Supervisor Anderson's petition for sunrise to sunset that we talked about. Any committment like this from our leaders is one step further away from seeing the repeat devestation of the evironment and fishing program at Loveland.Our communities need and deserve this evening access if they want it.    ----- Forwarded Message ----- From: Sleeper, Maggie <maggie.sleeper@sdcounty.ca.gov>To: Russell Walsh <russellwalsh2003@yahoo.com>Sent: Wednesday, August 7, 2024 at 03:23:31 PM PDTSubject: RE: [External] Please Read, Maggie, Loveland Sunrise to Sunset Petition.

Hi Russell,

  

Here is the petition: PETITION: Keep Loveland Reservoir Open From Sunrise to Sunset (sandiegocounty.gov)

  

Feel free to circulate it – we will add it into our communications Queue to go out in a future e-blast and on our social media pages.

Thanks,

Maggie

  

From: Russell Walsh <russellwalsh2003@yahoo.com>
Sent: Tuesday, July 23, 2024 4:53 PM
To: Sleeper, Maggie <Maggie.Sleeper@sdcounty.ca.gov>
Subject: [External] Please Read, Maggie, Loveland Sunrise to Sunset Petition.

  

Hi Maggie, 

  

I hope you and your family are doing great! 

  

Thank you for your efforts in utilizing  Supervisor Anderson's lakes initiative to reverse the recent threat of further reductions to the access at some of the east county area lakes. Your work has not gone unnoticed. The idea of Supervisor Anderson the COSD becoming involved in rural lakes is always popular.

  

One part of Supervisor Anderson's success with the recent threat of access loss was a petition.

  

Given Supervisor Anderson's many letters of support for Sunrise to Sunset access and other issues at Loveland Reservoir, combined with the inclusion of Sweetwater Authority lakes named in Supervisor Anderson's initiative and work by Brian Albright's Parks and Recreation,  I am hoping that Supervisor Anderson would consider spearheading a petition to open Loveland Reservoir from Sunrise to Sunset. I understand there is a possibility of the petition failing in the short term, which is undesirable. Still, it could get us out of the hopeless situation we are currently in regarding legal and practical access at the Loveland Reservoir for working people.

  

You may know that the non-profit, Friends of Loveland Reservoir's,  compromise to have volunteers close the gates at Sunset failed. Please consider a powerful petition for Sunrise to Sunset according to the easement as the credible land-use policy and next possible productive step.

  

As you have seen, Maggie, there is a growing coalition on lake access and improvements. I have been sharing what has been happening with the Lakes initiative since we met almost four years ago with these leading individuals and groups.  I believe this is a potential case of " a rising tide lifts all boats," which fits Supervisor Anderson's goals and recognition for his district's values and effort for outdoor enthusiasts. A petition for Loveland would be broadly recognized as further commitment to  Supervisor Anderson's commitment to rural area lakes for the broadest range of recreation and subsistence fishers. It would be inspirational to advocates that we both have seen as nearly hopeless in the face of losses at our lakes. 

  

Please help make this a reality. I am considering asking the individuals and groups who have begun to form a coalition on a better future for our rural lakes to initiate a petition. However, given your significant contributions to the Loveland cause, it's crucial to ask Supervisor Anderson's office to spearhead this and add willing groups as endorsers of the petition to open Loveland from Sunrise to Sunset. I can help recruit the various leading individuals and non-profits. 

  

Best regards,

  

Russell 

  

  

Russell Walsh

Jamul CA, 91935

subject: [External] Colorado Billionaire Shouldn’t Decide Our Safety - Say No to HGVS
body:
Dear Chair Lawson-Remer, board members and staff:

My family and myself have lived in Harmony Grove for 40 years. I’m a retired firefighter/ captain with over 30 years of experience. We’ve been through multiple big fires. It’s just a matter of time before another event happens. During the 2014 Cocos Fire, the wind changed directions and about 30 homes burned, and it took us almost two hours just to get a few miles out. Back then, the village site was just dirt, and even that helped slow the flames. Roads were jammed even with far fewer cars.

Now Harmony Grove Village is built (the community actually testified in favor of the project back in 2011). We love our new neighbors, but evacuations are going to be seriously constricted: so many vehicles trying to get out on the same narrow roads. Years ago the County told us the safe place for growth was north of the creek, near the old egg ranch which is why we supported HGV. South of the creek was a dead-end fire-prone bowl unless there’s a second way out. County even removed a proposed road to Del Dios Highway from the road plans. It’s the main reason none of us can get insurance – we’re surrounded by brush and no way out.

HGV South would add another 1000 cars onto the same routes that were gridlocked back in 2014. And to make things worse, the County felt it was ok to give a Colorado billionaire a waiver for secondary access in a bowl that has repeatedly caught fire throughout the years. The County never modeled a full community evacuation (even though we asked repeatedly); they looked only at the immediate project area. We had to fundraise and pay for an independent expert, and the verdict was sobering: entrapment is likely. His analysis showed that it would take seven hours or more to evacuate everyone, but fires arrive much sooner.

Our fire chief also recently acknowledged HGV South wouldn’t pass today’s standards without a secondary access. Please vote no on HGV South, or at least require real secondary access. Our safety has to come first.

Respectfully,
Greg Kaczur
9033 Harmony Grove Rd

Sent from my iPhone
rationale: Resident public comment to the Board of Supervisors, dated 2025-09-30, opposing Harmony Grove Village South. It is outside the date window and has no request terms or listed correspondents.

subject: Meeting w/ Supervisor Anderson - April 28th 11am
body:
Good evening Planning Group Chairs,

Andrew Hayes here with Supervisor Anderson. I want to thank each of you for sending me your response. I wanted to let you know that the date that works for the greatest number of the chairs is Monday, April 28th at 11:00am. That is the date the Supervisor would like to go ahead with. Recognizing that all may not be able to attend in person we will be offering a virtual option as well as the option for you to send a representative in the event the Chair is unable to attend (of course if the Vice-Chair would like to attend in addition to the Chair that is more than welcome).

The in-person meeting will be located at Supervisor Anderson’s El Cajon District office at: 475 W. Bradley Ave., El Cajon, Ca 92020.

In advance of the meeting, the Supervisor has requested that you send over any of the topics you’d like discussed or would like to bring to his attention as he want’s to be sure to make this the best use of your time.

I’m looking forward to seeing you all there on Monday, April 28th, 11:00am. Lastly, in the event you are unable to attend and also not able to send a representative, I’d be happy to schedule an appointment where I can come to your planning group meeting or meet with you so you can share your thoughts and ask questions.

Thank you all and please do not hesitate to contact me anytime.

subject: Stoney Oak Ranch Support
body:
I’m writing in support of Stoney Oaks Ranch ahead of the community planning group meeting tomorrow.

Stoney Oaks Ranch has been a little slice of heaven for my two girls. Almost 3 years ago, for my oldest’s 5th birthday we reached out about hosting our party there and she has been hooked ever since.

We have attended their once a week camps, summer camps, and take horse riding lessons as well.

My girls have learned skills they wouldn’t have learned had they not had people like Angie and Krystal leading the way to teach kids from a young age a deep appreciation for being outdoors, working with your hands, and caring for animals. Kids don’t just get to show up and play. They work hard and they learn. They learn about respect, and responsibility, how to work as a team, and even self confidence. And when it’s time to go home, they don’t want to leave because they are where children should be: outside, climbing in a treehouse, getting dirty, and exploring.

We live in a small home with a small yard and what my girls get to experience at Stoney Oaks is unique and something they can’t get by just walking into our own backyard. Certainly not the joy and therapeutic wonder of being around horses and other farm animals!

We’re so grateful for everyone at Stoney Oaks Ranch and our weekly schedule has felt empty without my kids being able to gather with other kids who share the same love of being outside and caring for animals.

We LOVE Stoney Oaks and give our full whole hearted support to everything they do.

Sincerely,
Vittoria Allen
rationale: Public comment supporting Stoney Oaks Ranch before a planning group meeting, dated 2024-04-03. Outside the window, with no request terms.

subject: Introducing Street Stewards - A grassroots initiative to keep San Diego’s street clean one block at a time!
body:
Dear East County Community Groups,

I am writing to inform you of a powerful new mapping tool developed specifically for San Diegans to help keep our streets clean together. My non-profit organization is called Street Stewards, and we are nearly 1,000 volunteers strong… and counting! We have developed a website where any San Diego County citizen can log in, find their local community, and adopt a block by recording litter pickups on our live interactive map.

Our powerful interactive map shows the health of the entire county’s streets with a color coded system which enables Stewards to decide to simply clean their own block OR go to where their efforts are needed most. Please see the attached graphics for an overview of how it works and an example of how our interactive map appears.

This website was developed with generous help from San Diego County’s Neighborhood Reinvestment Program grants, and it is a free tool for anyone to use! We would love your help in spreading the word about it with your membership, organization, and constituents. The strength of this model relies on participation and widespread adoption, so it is time to get the word out.

We are excited to collaborate to spread the word in your newsletters, emails, social media posts, and among your friends and colleagues! You can learn much more and sign up here: www.streetstewards.com. I am happy to provide more information, attend meetings and present, or explain further. Please don’t hesitate to get in touch with ideas about how to get the word out! Thank you for your time, and I look forward to working with you to make San Diego a more beautiful place - one block at a time.

Sincerely,

Aaron Null
Founder, Executive Director
Street Stewards
484-883-9476

subject: [External] Harmony Grove
body:
I just heard that you got that Harmony Grove development approved.  And without due consideration to traffic flow.  I understand you were somehow in charge of this project at the county?
   Yes, I read what you wrote.  But filling a page with words is very different from thinking first and writing useful information down.  You guys did not think.  And you did not go out and look at the real world.  I know you didn't because you said nothing about Via Rancho Parkway.  And a large percentage of the commuters from your new development are going to use Via Rancho Parkway to access I15.  How could you not see that?  It is already happening.
   A few years ago Citracado Parkway was widened from Auto Park down to West Valley Parkway.  So now a lot of people decided that they have a shortcut to bypass the truly awful 79 to I15 interchange during the rush hours.  They use the new Citracado Parkway.  But what happens when they get to West Valley Parkway?  The rest of Citracado does not go through to I15.  So they go west on West Valley Parkway, turn left on Via Rancho Parkway, and access I15 via that route.  I'm serious.  Since the northern part of Citracado opened, the traffic on Via Rancho Parkway has become truly awful.  Some people with driveways on that road, or who live on cross streets without street lights are effectively trapped in their homes for five hours a day.  Emergency vehicle access is almost non-existent during the busy rush "hours".  (Usually 2 or 3 hours morning and night.)  And now more people are pouring onto or off of I15 at the notoriously bad Via Rancho Parkway on ramp, which increases an already dangerous situation.
   Now, given that you din't think or look at the real world, I assume you probably have no idea what Via Rancho Parkway is like.  So let me tell you it would be REALLY expensive to widen so that it can handle the traffic that is currently being dumped onto it and the added traffic that your new development will dump onto it.  It is in rough country and would require significant excavation, retaining walls, culverts, and probably lots of eminent domain taking of land to make it work.  In short, it won't ever happen.
   So you have doomed people to die in traffic accidents or in their homes while awaiting emergency services due to your poor planning.  (And to the poor planning of whoever thought it was a good idea to finish only the one section of Citracado Parkway.)  Of course you will deny it, but you have.
   Now is there anything that can be done to mitigate the damage?  I think it's obvious:  put Citracado Parkway the rest of the way through to I15.  Go look at it.  You can do it on Google Earth if you don't want to leave your chair.  It is platted all the way through.  And it exists all the way through except for a very short stretch where it just stops abruptly.
   Look at this picture:

   The red arrow shows the end of the north section of Citracado.  Notice that the road is all widened and ready to use to that point.  The orange arrow shows the intersection on I15 that is called "Citracado Parkway".  It is there and ready to use.  The wobbly blue line that I drew shows where it appears to me that the road is supposed to continue on, eventually connecting to Gamble Lane, which I assume would then take the name Citracado as it becomes Citracado again when it passes beneath I15.  And if you look at where the yellow arrow is pointed, it looks like some clearing has even been done along this slightly curving route, though long enough ago that someone has planted a tree in the middle of it.
   Everything is in place to have Citracado extended through to I15.  So what can you do to help make that happen?  I'm sorry if you think I've been mean, but you didn't think, you did not do your due diligence, and you have created an even bigger problem than we already have by allowing this housing development.  I really do believe that people will crash and probably die due to this decision.  Or will die in their homes because emergency vehicles cannot get to them in a timely manner.  (Lest you think I'm exaggerating, it appears that my neighbor just died yesterday evening, even after calling an ambulance.  A lot of old people live off of Via Rancho Parkway.)  I think you owe it to us to at least try to mitigate the problem.

--Brian M. Godfrey
  brian@wildbirdshop.com <mailto:brian@wildbirdshop.com>
rationale: A member of the public complains about traffic from the Harmony Grove development, dated 2025-10-03. That is outside the window, and it has no reference to the request's people or terms.

Subject: SANDAG Vision Zero

Hello All,

Last week I met (zoom) with Staff from SANDAG re their Vision Zero Program. This program is still a work in progress and they estimate that it won’t be completed for at least the next few months.
Vision Zero<https://www.sandag.org/projects-and-programs/regional-initiatives/vision-zero>
sandag.org<https://www.sandag.org/projects-and-programs/regional-initiatives/vision-zero>
[cid:image001.png@01DAEDA7.62DC5860]<https://www.sandag.org/projects-and-programs/regional-initiatives/vision-zero>

Vision Zero is a comprehensive data driven program to identify roads/areas in our region that have the highest concentration of major accidents where law enforcement has been involved and reports have been generated.

With this accident information, these areas have then been analyzed to determine what changes or improvements could be made so that there could potentially be zero future accidents.

This information could then also be used by municipalities and the County to apply for approximately $1 billion dollars in federal grants.

One of the concerns that I have is that this data is 2 years behind, so the numbers are from 2022. It seems to me that after Covid, the public generally appears to be driving a lot faster and in a much more unsafe manner, hence an increase in accidents that these initial studies might not capture.

Below is a link for the SANDAG’s interactive map associated with this program. It shows the areas that have the highest concentration of accidents, amongst other data.
[cid:image002.jpg@01DAEDA7.62DC5860]
Traffic Safety Dashboard<https://opendata.sandag.org/stories/s/5f7y-nefe>
opendata.sandag.org<https://opendata.sandag.org/stories/s/5f7y-nefe>

While SANDAG’s goal for this program is to provide the data to help with grants, I see this as a great tool to use when we are asking DPW and TAC to reduce speeds and study roads in our area for traffic calming or other ways to reduce accidents.

I’ll keep you posted when I get further updates. If you have any questions, please let me know.

Best regards,

Eileen Delaney
Vice Chair, APG- San Diego County

Eileen Delaney, Chair
Fallbrook Planning Group
Fallbrook Design Review Board

Visit our website for current meeting information

subject: Alpine Community Planning Group Chair Walks like A Duck.
body:
Travis Lyon

Chair

Alpine Community Planning Group

With blind CC's

Hello,Travis , 

I am concerned about your refusal to write the letters of support from three months ago.   Supervisor Anderson has already given them and the massive overwhelming interest in sunrise to sunset  has been demonstrated many times before your own eyes, ears, heart and mind. 

 

In fact, anyone acting like you have, independently canceling many full ACPG votes since I started going advocating at ACPG meetings in 2022, with inaction on the motion passed and the devastating consequences,   would logically be considered a person with a terrible self-serving conflict of interest. 

What would start to change my mind is the letters of support that everybody in your group, including yourself,  and  except  Darlene Cossio of Friends of Loveland voted for. Did you make a deal with Darlene or somebody else to shelf the motion post vote? Is shelving things by yourself for whatever reason part of the ACPG’s foundation? 

Why do you think those letters of support would not benefit the grass roots Loveland Defenders and Advocates who solicited them? The community including the board members who voted for them. Supervisor Anderson’s constituents? Have you performed such dedicated service to Loveland? Do you fancy yourself  working Loveland Miracles for the community behind the scenes? You never did before now. 

I have a theory of what you are up to but would not like to expend the energy to confirm them yet. However, I will say this. I imagine you like to console yourself that I am rude without concern for your own rudeness as exemplified in canceling unanimous or near unanimous ACPG votes even though you leave the meetings , time and time again, with promises to fulfill them. Does the board not monitor you for these failures? What is legitimate about your leadership and defaulting on board votes? 

Please write and send the letters of support ASAP, as promised months ago,  with proof of service to deserving advocates. The timing of now is really important. 

Russell

subject: March 12th Board Hearing on Socially Equitable Cannabis Program
body:
On March 12, the Board will be hearing an item on the Socially Equitable Cannabis Program (please see attached PDF that describes the various components of the cannabis program).
Supervisor Anderson asked us to invite you to a District 2 unincorporated communities stakeholder meeting to provide you with the details of the upcoming Board vote on Tuesday, as well as the progress on other aspects of the County's cannabis policy.
Please let us know if you are available at 10 a.m. on Friday, March 8th to participate.
The Zoom link will be provided upon rsvp to gregory.kazmer@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:gregory.kazmer@sdcounty.ca.gov> .
As you may recall, on June 15, 2022 (7), the Board unanimously approved Supervisor Anderson's Board Letter with 16 measures to be included within the Cannabis Permitting Program Environmental Impact Report (EIR) and Socially Equitable Cannabis Program.
County staff provided Supervisor Anderson with a progress report on the community outreach and implementation the 16 measures, which we have attached for you.
The Supervisor's goal is always to provide transparency to you about what actions are coming before the Board of Supervisors and give you the opportunity to have your voice heard.
This meeting will provide the most up to date information on the County's Cannabis policy for the unincorporated areas, and how you can participate in the upcoming board meeting as well as the upcoming EIR process.
Thank you,

Greg Kazmer
Senior Land Use Advisor
District 2, Office of Joel Anderson

    Battery Energy Storage Systems Project

Battery Energy Storage Systems Project

Dear Interested Stakeholder,

We want to hear from you! The San Diego County Fire Protection District invites you to attend a public meeting to share your thoughts on the San Diego County Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) Best Practices Report (Report). BESS are technology designed to store and manage energy for later use. It typically uses rechargeable batteries to store energy from various sources, such as the electrical grid, renewable energy sources like solar or wind power, or other power generation methods. On September 11, 2024, the Board of Supervisors directed San Diego County Fire to develop a technical study with recommendations that consider setbacks from residential uses as well as best practice safety standards, including 2023 NFPA 855. The completed report can be accessed at the project website. County Staff is looking for your feedback on the recommended best practices, safety standards, and siting recommendations for new and existing BESS applications. PDS is hosting this virtual public meeting to receive your input on November 14, 2024, at 6:00 PM (registration link provided below).

Disability-related accommodations necessary to facilitate meeting participation, language interpretation, including American Sign Language, and written materials in alternative languages and formats are available upon request. Hi Travis! I’m a TV reporter for Spectrum News. The station is based in LA, but I live in and cover San Diego County for them! I’m working on a TV story on the Alpine County Park and the lawsuit that was just filed to stop it. I have an interview with someone on-camera who is against the park, but I am trying to find someone to interview on-camera who can talk about why they support it, so the story is balanced! I was chatting with the County, and since they are not allowed to comment on pending litigation, they thought you might be a good option for an interview since you spoke in favor of the project! If you are willing, we would just meet at the site and look around and talk about why it would be good for the community and why you support it! I shouldn’t need more than half hour or so, and this would be an on-camera pre-recorded interview that we would schedule sometime in February!

Let me know if you are interested, and if you are not, if you know of any other Alpine residents who support the project who might talk to me! Thank you so much!!!! Have a great night!

--
Bree Steffen

subject: Re: Sunrise to Sunset Discussion at Alpine Community Planning Group.
body:
Steve HalesDirector Friends of Loveland Reservoir

Hello Steve,

Steve, I want to express my sincere gratitude to you and your board for the commendable actions you've taken in support of Sunrise to Sunset. Your efforts have not gone unnoticed and are greatly appreciated. 

Have you reached out to Congressman Issa? Our easement is primarily a federal issue, and while we need follow-through, and community support everywhere we can get it, Congressman Issa is our strongest ally where the Forest Service is concerned. Please ask your board to promote a quality petition for progress on the restoration of  Sunrise to Sunset access ASAP.  As you said recently, agencies like to work with and respond to groups like Friends of Loveland Reservoir. If you need help, please let me and others know, perhaps via membership and a website.  

Your help at the ACPG is important:The ACPG has been a good base at times for Loveland Advocacy but there have been let downs too. Your board members know that  I went to a half dozen meetings with the Alpine Community Planning group for help with Loveland in the year before it was drained and to many meetings since. In the spring of 2022 a strong vote passed by ACPG to encourage Sweetwater to come to the Alpine Group. There was a least one previous resolution to write letters of support on recreation themes.  However, the chair did not complete these tasks despite the strong votes. The same thing appears to be happening with April's nearly unanimous vote for a letter of support from the ACPG on the Sunrise to Sunset. I believe you are aware through CC'd email on this trajectory. We need to work together so the ACPG honors community work and interests at Loveland and the work of the people on the planning advisory board itself on behalf of Loveland Reservoir so we can have success on Sunrise to Sunset and full defense of future complete dewatering which are here. We all agree that land use organizations are falling short of legal easement adherence and should be advised and strenuously petitioned to do otherwise. 

Please check your emails from me about Sweetwater's goal to float 200 acres of solar panels at Sweetwater Reservoir. 

The minimum water levels to float that industrial-type project will likely come from Loveland Reservoir and create new cyclical dewatering episodes. Sweetwater refuses to remove the threat, which is a factor. The good news is that it is being challenged locally in South Bay and here by us. 

Appreciatively,

Russell

Russell Walsh

4639 Montiel Truck Trail

Jamul CA, 91935

Steve

Director Friends of Loveland

CC Karen Wood Executive Director Friends of Loveland

  

  

Steve,

  

I am following up on your letter from April regarding FOLR support for Sunrise to Sunset at Loveland Reservoir.

As we near the point of longest day length in the summer of 2024 I am curious as to progress made, or effort given for our nature viewer and other recreation users on this matter. 

  

Also, I have advised you about how Sweetwater Authority is a constant applicant and recipient of State and Federal grants, yet is comfortable shortchanging taxpayers and citizens on even the limited sunrise to sunset access to Loveland's shoreline. You told me that FOLR supports that. How can we work together to challenge this taxpayer inequity so that FOLR followers and all other lake users may experience the therapeutic recreation and sometimes food aquistion rights they own at  Loveland Reservoir.

  

Thank you for you work for  nature lovers , fishers and hikers who need this recreation and proper voice and action in our communities by our leaders. I have letters of support on Sunrise to Sunset from Supervisor Anderson if you can use that in you advocacy. The ACPG was almost unaniously in favor of a letter of support to Sweetwater and the Forest Service on Sunrise to Sunset a few months ago, with the FOLR member being the only one to abstain. However , it appears the Chair has not notified or responded to concerns about the creation and issue of that letter. Please follow up on that with Chair Travis Lyon. 

  

Russell Walsh

On Friday, April 12, 2024 at 03:33:03 PM PDT, Steve Hales <steve@hales.xyz> wrote:

  

  

Russell,

 

The FOLR board supports sunrise to sunset hours at Loveland.

 

You are incorrect about what happened at the ACPG meeting.  In Darlene’s position as a member of the ACPG board, she abstained from voting on the motion – but she did not vote “No” or try to “block” it as you say.  And she abstained only after it was obvious the motion would pass anyway.

 

Regardless, Darlene can vote however she likes as a member of the ACPG board, without FOLR approving or justifying that vote. 

 

I hope this clarifies the misunderstanding.

 

Steve

Subject: Sunrise to Sunset Discussion at Alpine Communiity Planning Group.

 

 

 

Karen Wood

Executive Director 

Friends of Loveland Reservoir

Alpine CA

 

Hello  Karen,

 

Thank you for your recent complimentary work on the Loveland fishing float platform and other items of concern for Loveland Lake users. 

 

During the Alpine community planning group meeting last week, a significant issue regarding access to Loveland Reservoir was raised. Your board member, Darlene Cossio,  who is also on the planning group board, attempted to block the group's motion for a letter of support  to Sweetwater Authority and the US Forest Service for sunrise-to-sunset access. She claimed that the issue was already being addressed.

 

Would you please clarify what your board members' actions and comments mean for restoring access at Loveland according to the easement? Why does your board member see this being resolved so that she would block a letter of support and make the statements I am asking about?

 

Another spring and summer of afternoon and early evening recreation at Loveland is slipping away from working people and their families. Please support independent advocates in requesting that the ACPG bring the Cleveland National Forest administrators back to the ACPG meeting for a public follow-up on our meeting with them at the ACPG  last October. 

 

Appreciatively,

 

Russell

subject: Re: We Still Need An Advocate.
body:
Randy Moore

US Chief Forester

1400 Independence Ave. 

Washington DC 20250-0003

Dear Chief Moore,
The public in the region of Loveland Reservoir in the Cleveland National Forest are in great need of your  long-standing resolution to public service. 

I am writing to follow up on our recent local non-profit Friends of Loveland Reservoir to Forest Service contact regarding Sunrise to Sunset access and the compatibility of the easement-protected "shoreline"  fishing program with Sweetwater Authority's water licenses and California environmental and water regulations. 

As you will see from this 4 year old email chain, this is something I was pleading for your help with and trying to help the Forest Service understand as far back as September 2020.

It is clear from the easement, land swap origination documents, and past  Forest Service oversight of Loveland Reservoir that volunteers are not a factor in the public's right and need to access the hiking, fishing, and birdwatching program.  I don't agree with the pursuit of such a program of volunteers, or with exposing Loveland recreation users to the risk of failure of it and another lengthy setback on therapeutic recreation and subsistence fishing for lower-income earners in the region.

Sweetwater is simply obligated by the land swap and easement to provide access to the lake until sunset 365 days a year. Supervision during those hours, or lack thereof, is Sweetwater's business, not that of citizens, or the US Forest Service.  This is all 100% legally unambiguous. Please call out your legal department’s claims otherwise and/or have that analysis reviewed by another independent agency.

Fortunately, others in the community are stepping up. Please create a path for remedies to having lost much of Loveland's public benefits since our earlier failed communications and failure to implement the protection and remedies at Loveland that so many of us have petitioned Supervisor Tangenberg to act on for so many years now. 

Sincerely,

Russell Walsh

4639 Montiel Truck Trail

Jamul CA, 91935

619-922-6235

    On Friday, September 18, 2020 at 08:35:44 AM PDT, Russell Walsh <russellwalsh2003@yahoo.com> wrote:

  Mr. Tangenberg,

Thank you for that email. Why would you want to renew the agreement other than to weaken what is already a substantially good easement as far as hours of access if it were respected? What terms are being considered for renewal? The lake fishing program is small but in geographical terms relative to the overall size of the lake, and then when the Sweetwater Authority drains it to send water the their other reservoir downstream it becomes even smaller.

Now I hear from Sweetwater Authority board meetings that they are considering lowering the lake below emergency levels. Are you aware of what the means for the fishing program? I would like to know . I would like to know that you are watching out for us on these items and are willing to fight for the U.S public.

The Sweetwater Authority does not have an elected representative in the area or the Reservoir and they can not be made to give a damn about the people who use the lake other than in court and I just can't do that.

Thank you,

Russell Walsh
     On Friday, September 18, 2020, 07:39:23 AM PDT, Tangenberg, Scott R -FS <scott.tangenberg@usda.gov> wrote:

 Mr. Walsh,My understanding is that the Sweetwater Authority is continuing to consider ways in which they can safely administer their fishing program more than 3 days per week.  As I said in my last note, we will work with them to renew our agreement once our current emergencies reach some new level of resolution.
If you still feel compelled to contact my supervisor, his name is Randy Moore, Region 5 Regional Forester, and he can be reached at randy.moore@usda.gov.

To: Tangenberg, Scott R -FS <scott.tangenberg@usda.gov>
Subject: Re: Referals To Your Supervisor and To A 'Whistle Blower"Contact. Mr. Tangenberg ,

You give way too much credit on this issues to the Sweetwater Authority and way to little to me and the public you represent. Because of this you come across as a real kiss up kick down kind of guy, one with blinders on who can not or will not see that the Sweetwater Authority is scamming the public . You don't work for the politcal/business interests in the region first and the public second. You have it backwards. Sweetwater Authorty is the worst lake of many in our region on returning rights as social distancing has relaxed for recreation and as public health prerogatives by the leadership, other than you, in our broader communities have shifted toward enabling outdoor activity.

You are already to forgive the Sweetwater Authorities obligations on the basis of the Valley fire , for as long as they want that and the fire didn't even reach Loveland. I know because it ripped through my property and was contained before it got there. The lake can be operated 7 days a week sunrise to sunset , no problem. Please quit giving it away like some lackey for the Political and Business entity that the Sweetwater Authority is.

You told me that all those request I made went directly back to you. So, I have never had appropriate contact with any level above yours to deal with this issue. So, it is you job as an honorable personIt to tell your supervisors at the National and other Levels that I have lost faith in you and that I should have recourse above you. I certainly do not want to work with anyone under your authority. such as a Descanso ranger,

If the leadership in your organization approves of how you lied to me and played pawn to the Sweetwater Authority , we really do have traitors in the government. My feeling is no one has much knowledge of what is happening but you and I . That needs to change.

Please do what I asked.

Russell Walsh
On Monday, September 14, 2020, 10:20:37 AM PDT, Tangenberg, Scott R -FS <scott.tangenberg@usda.gov> wrote:

Mr. Walsh,
I've been as clear as I can be in my previous communications.  Sweetwater Authority has the jurisdiction on access to Loveland Reservoir.  While a public access easement exists, our partner knows best during these trying times how access can be facilitated.  The Cleveland National Forest (and every National Forest in California) is currently closed to public access given the extreme fire risk and dangerous fire conditions.  The Valley Fire burn area will be closed for some time in the future as well.

All that said, I've cc'd Bob Heiar, our District Ranger for the Descanso Ranger District, and the local manager for this part of the Forest.  He has expressed to me an interest in revisiting the expired agreement with Sweetwater Authority sometime in the future, in order to reaffirm that commitment and establish a good arrangement for continued access and opportunities for the public there.

As to your question about supervisor contact or whistle-blower reporting, you have already been in contact with both our National and Regional Offices, and your concerns have been referred to me. When conditions change, regarding COVID, fires, fire weather, and the extreme challenges managing through these, I will do everything I can to safely re-establish access for our public.

subject: RE: Objective Design Standards (ODS) Checklist - Alpine
body:
Good morning,

Thank you for your continued coordination with our Objective Design Standards (ODS) project. As discussed, State laws that are already in effect require that any housing developments eligible for streamlining approval be reviewed with clear, objective standards regarding design aspects such as materials, colors, etc. Typically, these would be projects that include affordable housing units.  Design standards that are not objective cannot be applied to these projects.

To ensure we have objective design standards available for any potential applications, our team used your existing Design Review Checklist as a template to create an Objective Design Review Checklist that clarifies any subjective language and maintains the visual integrity of housing developments in your community. We kindly request your group send any feedback on the checklist by August 15th, 2024.

The Objective Design Review Checklist will serve as a supplemental form for projects eligible for streamlined approval under state law. It will not replace the current Design Review Checklist<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/dam/sdc/pds/drb/AlpineDesignReviewChecklistFINAL1.pdf>, which will continue to apply to projects not eligible for the streamlined review. While no applications for this streamlined process have been submitted in your Community Planning Area, the Objective Design Review Checklist will be applicable if one is received. We are finalizing this Objective Design Review Checklist and will make it easily accessible online for potential applications eligible for these State laws.

Attached is the draft Objective Design Review version of your community’s existing Design Review Checklist, and a map delineating potentially eligible areas for this streamlined process. A strikethrough indicates a proposed removal of language, while an underline indicates a proposed change/addition.  Also attached is a PDF version for your reference. There may also be highlighted language or comment bubbles that we are requesting specific feedback on, regarding unclear language or unclear measurements.  There are additional details in the original e-mail below.

We will work to incorporate your suggestions into the checklist which will be accessible on our website in Fall 2024. While there is some flexibility to make changes in the future, staff availability and allocation may make it challenging to respond urgently to suggestions for edits after that date. Therefore, please ensure you submit any requests for modifications by August 15th, 2024, so your feedback can be incorporated into the checklist before it is made available online.

Please let us know if you have any questions as you review the document. We appreciate your continued collaboration and commitment to enhancing our unincorporated communities.

[cid:image001.png@01DA7ABA.EF015A80]<http://www.sdcpds.org/>
Luis Duran
Planner III | Planning & Development Services | Long Range Planning
County of San Diego | 5510 Overland Ave. Suite 310 | San Diego, CA 92123|
• (619) 214-4698  |  • Luis.Duran@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:Luis.Duran@sdcounty.ca.gov>

From: Duran, Luis
Sent: Friday, March 22, 2024 4:03 PM
To: travislyonacpg@gmail.com
Subject: Objective Design Standards (ODS) Checklist - Alpine

Hello Chair Lyon,

I hope this email finds you well. Following our recent presentation at your Community Planning Group (CPG) meeting on February 22, 2024. I am pleased to update you on the latest progress regarding the Objective Design Standards (ODS) project.

To recap, our presentation centered around State laws which allow for a streamlined process for eligible multifamily projects, and how design standards can be implemented in that process. Eligible projects need to meet all eligibility requirements and objective design standards at the time of application, or their development cannot be streamlined through a ministerial process. Our project team is working to edit your existing Design Review Checklist to clarify any subjective language to maintain the visual integrity of your community in the case an eligible project application is submitted. Attached is a draft “Objective” version of the Alpine Checklist with a corresponding map, delineating potentially eligible areas for streamlined housing development.

A few notes as you review the attached documents:

MAP: State law states that a multifamily development “contains two or more residential units”.  According to the California Department of Housing and Community Development, a new single-family development and an attached accessory dwelling unit when built together are considered multifamily and are eligible for streamlining under SB 35.  An applicant would still need to meet all eligibility requirements to streamline their project. These eligible parcels are distinguished by a pink color.  The blue parcels are eligible for streamlining under State law, where three or more units can be built under current Zoning. The attached maps have been updated to reflect recent State laws in effect as of March 2024.

CHECKLIST: Attached is a Microsoft Word document containing tracked changes.  A strikethrough indicates a proposed removal of language, while an underline indicates proposed change/addition.  Also attached is a PDF version for your reference. The Design Review Checklist for your community may include goals or intentions related to your original Design Guidelines. As this draft is for ease of use, we have removed these to strictly focus on the design standards that must be followed. This makes the checklist shorter and easier to read. There may also be highlighted language or comment bubbles that we are requesting specific feedback on, regarding unclear language or unclear measurements.

As discussed previously, this project will not be updating or changing Alpine’s Form Based Code (FBC).  The Draft Objective Design Standards Checklist attached is for the areas not covered by the FBC.  We kindly request your group review the attached Checklist to ensure that it accurately reflects the intent of your existing community’s design standards. Please submit your initial feedback no later than April 23rd, 2024.

We appreciate your collaboration and commitment to enhancing our unincorporated communities.

For further information on ODS, please visit the following links: Objective Design Standards | Engage San Diego County<https://engage.sandiegocounty.gov/ods> and Objective Design Standards (sandiegocounty.gov)<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/pds/longrangeplanning/ods/>

subject: SANDAG Vision Zero
body:
Hello All,

Last week I met (zoom) with Staff from SANDAG re their Vision Zero Program. This program is still a work in progress and they estimate that it won’t be completed for at least the next few months.
Vision Zero
sandag.org

Vision Zero is a comprehensive data driven program to identify roads/areas in our region that have the highest concentration of major accidents where law enforcement has been involved and reports have been generated.

With this accident information, these areas have then been analyzed to determine what changes or improvements could be made so that there could potentially be zero future accidents.

This information could then also be used by municipalities and the County to apply for approximately $1 billion dollars in federal grants.

One of the concerns that I have is that this data is 2 years behind, so the numbers are from 2022. It seems to me that after Covid, the public generally appears to be driving a lot faster and in a much more unsafe manner, hence an increase in accidents that these initial studies might not capture.

Below is a link for the SANDAG’s interactive map associated with this program. It shows the areas that have the highest concentration of accidents, amongst other data.
Traffic Safety Dashboard
opendata.sandag.org

While SANDAG’s goal for this program is to provide the data to help with grants, I see this as a great tool to use when we are asking DPW and TAC to reduce speeds and study roads in our area for traffic calming or other ways to reduce accidents.

I’ll keep you posted when I get further updates. If you have any questions, please let me know.
Best regards,

Eileen Delaney
Vice Chair, APG- San Diego County

Eileen Delaney, Chair

body:
Robin :)

Questions from APG members:

Response - I am still working on this answer..

       Via

Sent from the all new AOL app for iOS

On Saturday, July 27, 2024, 9:00 AM, APG <associationofplanninggroups@gmail.com> wrote:

Good Morning APG Members,
Note: At the July 26, 2024 SANDAG Board of Directors meeting there was no (zero) County representation. This means we had no one representing the Unincorporated Area with the power to vote. Nora Vargas was absent. Joel Anderson was absent. The County Board of Supervisors has two alternates: Terra Lawson-Remer and Monica Montgomery Steppe. Neither were present. When a vote was taken to consider borrowing $20 million of future Transnet funds for the "Transnet Regional Bike Early Action Program" there was no one from the County to vote. We had an empty seat.
SANDAG's CEO, Mario Orso:
Mario Orso reported that SANDAG would continue to provide updates to the Board and stakeholders on the priority corridors of SR 78 and SR 67. He did not include SRs 76, 79 or 94 in this priority list. The Transnet Independent Taxpayer Oversight Committee is seeking community members for their Board. Information located at their website: https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/transnet-independent-taxpayer-oversightSANDAG will not hold Board of Director meetings in August, but staff and working groups will continue with work.

APG comment to Board: This month we held the first Evacuation Tour with SANDAG and Caltrans staff. The potential evacuation routes in the Ramona area were thoroughly explored and wildfire hazards such as chimney fire burn zones were identified for the group by our local fire behavior expert, Dan Summers. The next Evacuation Tour will explore the SR 94 corridor from Campo to Jamul; including the dangerous intersection of Otay Lakes and Honey Springs Road. The Unincorporated Community values these opportunities to partner with SANDAG and Caltrans to share vital boots-on-the-ground knowledge in order to develop safe evacuation routes for all travelers in the region. Thank you.
California Transportation Commission (CTC):Two CTC Commissioners introduced themselves and reported that they are "the money people" for State and Federal transportation funds. Commissioners Clarissa Reyes Falcon and Lee Ann Eager invited Board members to attend an upcoming meeting being held in San Diego from August 15-16. Website for information: https://catc.ca.gov/meetings-events/commission-meetings-2024

Transnet Oversight Annual Report and Performance Audit and Budget:The overall feedback from the Board to those presenting on Transnet funds and projects was that there was a clear lack of information and accountability is needed. Cost Benefit Analysis was missing. Staff reported miniscule use of the public transportation options and utilization of biking or walking - Return On Investment is dismal. SANDAG often quotes the maxim that limited funds should be used to help the most people. Historically, the Transnet funds are benefitting very few. As of FY 2023, total bikeway Program funding was $397.3 million. Transnet funds represented $187.2 million (47%) of this spending. The promise of the Transnet funds to improve public safety through corridor projects is not being met. SANDAG staff's explanation was that the voters had an expectation and the funding sources for these projects (of which Transnet funds are only one part/source) come with stipulations that are often in conflict with what the voters expected. This is the difficult environment in which planning and funding for projects exists.
Melanie Burkholder, City of Carlsbad comment: We need cost benefit analysis for these Transnet dollar projects.
Mario Orso, SANDAG CEO comment: We are working toward structural change in order to provide cost benefit analysis and demonstrate a good use of the funds

Lesa Heebner, City of Solana Beach comment: I know that many people leave my city to move east because it is more affordable. This puts more people on those roads and they need to be improved.
APG Comment to Board: What are the raw numbers for this conclusion that bike ridership has increased 5x? Does this conclusion represent a change from 50 to 500 riders, 50 to 5,000? We need to see the numbers. And, do you see a slower increase in pedestrian travel than expected due to e-bike encounters on pathways?
SANDAG response (Omar Atayee): Those are great questions. We don't have those numbers, but will get those to the Board. We don't know if e-bikes are impacting our numbers, but we are seeing an increase. I don't know if we have data on that.
Dawn Vettes, SANDAG CFO comment: We acknowledge room for improvement and are working to strengthen internal controls. Our next audit in 2027 will show significant progress.

SANDAG's Youth Opportunity Pass:In response to a previous Board question about the cost per ride of those utilizing the Youth Opportunity Pass, Mario Orso reported .69 cents was the average cost.
Questions from APG members:
Question - Is SANDAG informed of freeway projects in the County? Or, are freeway projects strictly a state affair? Does SANDAG have a role in the scheduling and decision making?Response - I am still working on this answer.....
News: Link to the Traffic Safety Dashboard https://www.sandag.org/trafficsafety. It is located in SANDAG’s Open Data Portal.
Original SANDAG documents and meeting minutes are available directly from SANDAG's Board of Directors website: https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/board-of-directors

Equitable Program DEIR.

>
>
> *SANDAG Board Actions and Discussions - March 2024*
>
> *SANDAG Retreat 2024:*
> March 8th meeting - a Board Retreat held at the Salt Drift Pointe, 536
> 13th Street, Imperial Beach from 8:30 to 3:30. Both the APG Representative
> (Robin Maxson) and Alternate (Eileen Delaney) attended and participated in
> the team building activities. The goal of the Retreat was to build a
> regional planning mindset for the Board members and to develop a set of
> criteria/traits for the next SANDAG CEO. Recruiting and interviewing has
> narrowed the candidate field to six individuals.
>
> *Caltrans:*
> Roy Abboud and Mario Orso - communicated to the APG Rep that Caltrans had
> 2.6 billion in funding for the unincorporated area projects. Also, that
> they would be "speeding up" projects on the SR 67.
>
> *125 Toll Road Action Plan:*
> March 22nd Meeting - Coleen Clementson reported that SANDAG had signed the
> contract with the group (unnamed) that would be running the new back-office
> system and that it would be up and running by the end of the year.
> Independent Performance Auditor - Courtney Ruby will be presenting the
> results of the audit at the next Board meeting. (As it turned out a Special
> SANDAG Board meeting was called for March 29th to specifically discuss the
> results of this internal audit.)
> Report on options discussed with South Bay leaders for early pay off of
> 125 Toll Road would be brought forth in a future meeting.
>
> March 29 Special Board Meeting - The report from the Office of the
> Independent Performance Auditor released a report on March 25th resulted in
> a Special meeting of the Board to be called.  This report was previously
> sent to APG members in a separate email, but here is the link:
> https://www.sandag.org/-/media/SANDAG/Documents/PDF/about/office-of-the-independent-performance-auditor/reports-and-documents/sr-125-investigation-report-final.pdf
>
> The report revealed ongoing, egregious lack of oversight and a pattern of
> failure to take action to correct a multitude of issues with operation of
> the 125 Toll Road.
> Board members questioned every aspect contributing to this situation:
> Why wasn't the Board informed of the back-office discrepancies in tolls
> collected and toll user accounts?
> Why have we signed a contract with the same company that did not deliver
> on the contractual requirements?
> Why would we contract again with companies that did not collect nor record
> tolls correctly?
> What is the criteria for selecting a company for the contract?
> Why wasn't it reported to the Board that tolls stopped being collected due
> to equipment disconnect sooner?
> Why is SANDAG using QuickBooks for accounting purposes?
> Who in SANDAG's executive leadership knew of these issues and when?
> What is SANDAG's Whistle Blower policy?
> Why did SANDAG allow a culture of intimidation to exist with respect to
> the former CEO?
> Why were financial reports repeatedly corrected and the issues leading to
> faulty numbers not corrected instead?
> How much money has the contractor been paid for the 125 Toll Road and for
> other projects they manage, for example the I-15 managed lanes.
> How can we ensure that the same accounting issues have not occurred with
> the I-15?
> How much money in tolls was lost overall?
>
> Board member comments were:
> "After I pick up my jaw from the floor I have a few questions."
> "This isn't just a black eye for SANDAG, but two black eyes."
> "We need to investigate potential fraud."
> "We need to rebuild trust in SANDAG."
>
> The Independent Performance Auditor's recommendations were accepted by the
> Board and more Board actions and answers to questions and concerns would be
> forthcoming at the April 12th regular Board meeting.
>
> *Report of SANDAG's Draft Fiscal Year 2025 Budget Program - Capital
> Projects:*
> SANDAG reported on the DRAFT FY 2025 Budget. The presentation included the
> project and funding allocation of both TransNet and non-TransNet funded
> projects. The hand out (see attachment) was a visual overview of the
> projects and location - Note the lack of projects planned (funded) in the
> unincorporated area of the County. Based on this discrepancy in funding for
> the unincorporated area and for areas of North County the Board heard many
> complaints from its own members.
>
> APG comment to Board: "Good morning. Thank you. Representing the
> unincorporated area where we're 500 thousand strong. I understand that we
> use the limited funds where it can do the most good. But I would like to
> remind everyone to keep in mind that we do have a large population outside
> of the populated corridor. And, that in addition to the 500 thousand, we do
> have thousands of visitors on the weekends. So, I see a lot of funding for
> bikeways which is good for health and greenhouse gas reduction. But I see
> very limited funding for our Vision Zero Plan to reduce highway severe
> injuries and fatalities. I don't see a lot of money in the unincorporated
> area where all of the visitors are coming on the weekends and where there
> is a tremendous amount of pressure on those roadways. Also, I don't see
> that a priority is being given to wildfire evacuation. And, with two
> unsuccessful wildfire evacuations in '03 and '07 it is not a matter of if;
> but when we will have another one. Right now it is green, but it won't be
> that situation in June. I would like to know how SANDAG determines the
> funding allocation - how do they decide that balance between a population
> that is concentrated and a population that is spread out? Yet there is
> still a need in both areas. And, I do appreciate all of your work, but I
> want to understand how that calculus is made. Thank you."
>
> Susan Huntington (SANDAG staff) response: The annual budget really looks
> toward the Regional Plan prioritization process. So the Regional Plan is
> our long term plan and it establishes the implementation schedule of the
> projects. We use multiple different criterias in that project
> prioritization process. The annual budget looks at when those projects are
> meant to be open; like if a project is meant to be open in 2035 we need to
> get started on that project in say 2025. So, we're really looking to
> implement the Regional Plan as we pull the budget together. And, all of
> those criteria for prioritization come through the Regional Plan process."
>
> You can also view my comment at the meeting link:
> https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=arKeg7IFk7w   02:06:30
> and here is the link to the budget document:
> https://www.sandag.org/-/media/SANDAG/Documents/PDF/funding/budget/sandag-program-budget-fy-2025.pdf#page=6
>
> *SANDAG's Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA):*
> Report on RHNA from Sacramento's Housing and Community Development (HCD)
> staff Megan Kirkeby and Marisa Prasse.
> The HCD reported that future development continued to be focused on
> population corridors and not near open spaces or places without
> transportation options. This effectively eliminates rural and semi-rural
> areas for housing.
> Board discussion on the increased legislation from Sacramento (SB 35 and
> SB 423) that punished/fined cities for not meeting their RHNA numbers.
> Cities reported that Sacramento was applying a state-wide housing solution
> to individual cities instead of allowing a more reasonable and attainable
> allocation to be made regionally as some communities had more buildable
> land available than others.  Some unincorporated communities are located
> near job centers and should not be dismissed as potential housing locations
> due to a lack of public transit options.
>
> *APG Update:*
> In addition to this SANDAG report the APG has received acceptance of our
> Associate membership (non-voting) invitation to Community Sponsor Groups by
> Bonsall (Jennifer Haider), Jacumba (Cherry Diefenbach) and Twin Oaks Valley
> (Joseph Bunn). We will formally accept their membership at our June 1st APG
> meeting. Welcome to Bonsall, Jacumba and Twin Oaks Valley!
>
> Report Submitted by:
> Robin Joy Maxson, Representative to SANDAG
> Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County
>

body:
Hi Travis,

Hope this email finds you well! The County of San Diego's Land Use & Environment Group (LUEG) is conducting a series of public meetings from May 20 - June 4 to gather public feedback and input on an upcoming Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) on a $9 million ARPA-funded grant program to help address broadband access and affordability in unincorporated communities. This is a continuation of public engagement activities that helped inform the Comprehensive Broadband Plan<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/lueg/broadband/> released January 2023. We are inviting Alpine Community Planning Group to participate in this process.

The County is seeking public input on the criteria and scoring for the grant awards that were recently released via a draft Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA)<https://engage.sandiegocounty.gov/broadband>. There are a couple ways your community members can provide their feedback:

  1.  Attending one of the scheduled in-person public meetings (meeting flyer attached) or virtual webinar (details forthcoming)

We kindly ask you to help circulate this information with your network. All public comments on the draft NOFA are due by June 10th.

The County has contracted Guidehouse, a management consulting firm, to assist in this effort. subject: Feasibility Study Interview Request - California State Water Resources Control Board
body:
Good afternoon,

My name is Marissa, with Katz & Associates, and I'm part of a team under the California State Water Resources Control Board that is studying the feasibility of consolidating properties with individual groundwater wells or independent water systems east of Alpine with the Padre Dam Municipal Water District.

I'm reaching out today to see if you're interested in participating in an interview that will inform a Feasibility Study.

Background
The California State Water Resources Control Board<https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/> (Board) under the Safe and Affordable Funding for Equity and Resilience (Safer) Drinking Water Program<https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/water_issues/programs/grants_loans/sustainable_water_solutions/safer.html>, is funding planning efforts, including a Feasibility Study (Study), to support communities and help ensure a safe and reliable water supply for the future.

Due to some water quality concerns of existing groundwater wells in the Willowside Terrace community, located just east of the city of Alpine, the Board is conducting a Study to determine if this community can be connected to the Padre Dam Municipal Water District<https://www.padredam.org/> (PDMWD) to ensure a high quality, reliable and sustainable water supply is available for the future.

The Study team is interested in forming an expanded study area to include additional properties near Willowside Terrace that also use an independent water system reliant on groundwater.

As the Alpine Community Planning Group, the Study team is interested in participating in an interview with you to gather insights into the communities east of Alpine, near the potential study area. The Study team is interested in a range of views, opinions and experiences about independent water systems, the services provided by PDMWD, and the possibility of consolidating independent water systems with the district

Please let me know if you are interested in participating in an interview and what your availability looks like for the next few weeks.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Marissa Twite (she/her/hers)

subject: Sequan Truck Trail Potential Battery Storage Project
body:
Dear Mr. Lyon,

We were at last weeks (9/26/24) Alpine Planning Group meeting.  We would like you to add our emails to your list for any updates on progression of this very impractical venture.  Living in one of the highest fire zones and living on a street where we only have one way in and one way out, it seems so dangerous and illogical to approve a project like this.  It seemed apparent that after additional information at the meeting, it would not be an “if” there was a fire but “when” there would be a fire.  Additionally, if there was one, the water with the chemicals released would have unknown effects on our ground water, being that we are all on wells.  It’s extremely challenging to get fire insurance, and we can’t fathom how that will be affected.  Our assets are completely tied up in the value of our land and home, and fear this would be greatly compromised.
We know you heard the group loud and clear and hope your responses will reflect our great concern for this permit to be approved.

Thank you for your support on our behalf.

Sincerely,

Craig and Karen Knox

subject: Objective Design Standards (ODS) Checklist - Alpine
body:
Hello Chair Lyon,

I hope this email finds you well. Following our recent presentation at your Community Planning Group (CPG) meeting on February 22, 2024. I am pleased to update you on the latest progress regarding the Objective Design Standards (ODS) project.

To recap, our presentation centered around State laws which allow for a streamlined process for eligible multifamily projects, and how design standards can be implemented in that process. Eligible projects need to meet all eligibility requirements and objective design standards at the time of application, or their development cannot be streamlined through a ministerial process. Our project team is working to edit your existing Design Review Checklist to clarify any subjective language to maintain the visual integrity of your community in the case an eligible project application is submitted. Attached is a draft “Objective” version of the Alpine Checklist with a corresponding map, delineating potentially eligible areas for streamlined housing development.

A few notes as you review the attached documents:

MAP: State law states that a multifamily development “contains two or more residential units”.  According to the California Department of Housing and Community Development, a new single-family development and an attached accessory dwelling unit when built together are considered multifamily and are eligible for streamlining under SB 35.  An applicant would still need to meet all eligibility requirements to streamline their project. These eligible parcels are distinguished by a pink color.  The blue parcels are eligible for streamlining under State law, where three or more units can be built under current Zoning. The attached maps have been updated to reflect recent State laws in effect as of March 2024.

CHECKLIST: Attached is a Microsoft Word document containing tracked changes.  A strikethrough indicates a proposed removal of language, while an underline indicates proposed change/addition.  Also attached is a PDF version for your reference. The Design Review Checklist for your community may include goals or intentions related to your original Design Guidelines. As this draft is for ease of use, we have removed these to strictly focus on the design standards that must be followed. This makes the checklist shorter and easier to read. There may also be highlighted language or comment bubbles that we are requesting specific feedback on, regarding unclear language or unclear measurements.

As discussed previously, this project will not be updating or changing Alpine’s Form Based Code (FBC).  The Draft Objective Design Standards Checklist attached is for the areas not covered by the FBC.  We kindly request your group review the attached Checklist to ensure that it accurately reflects the intent of your existing community’s design standards. Please submit your initial feedback no later than April 23rd, 2024.

We appreciate your collaboration and commitment to enhancing our unincorporated communities.

For further information on ODS, please visit the following links: Objective Design Standards | Engage San Diego County<https://engage.sandiegocounty.gov/ods> and Objective Design Standards (sandiegocounty.gov)<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/content/sdc/pds/longrangeplanning/ods/>

Hello,Travis , 

I am concerned about your refusal to write the letters of support from three months ago.   Supervisor Anderson has already given them and the massive overwhelming interest in sunrise to sunset  has been demonstrated many times before your own eyes, ears, heart and mind. 

 

In fact, anyone acting like you have, independently canceling many full ACPG votes since I started going advocating at ACPG meetings in 2022, with inaction on the motion passed and the devastating consequences,   would logically be considered a person with a terrible self-serving conflict of interest. 

What would start to change my mind is the letters of support that everybody in your group, including yourself,  and  except  Darlene Cossio of Friends of Loveland voted for. You never did before now. 

I have a theory of what you are up to but would not like to expend the energy to confirm them yet. However, I will say this. I imagine you like to console yourself that I am rude without concern for your own rudeness as exemplified in canceling unanimous or near unanimous ACPG votes even though you leave the meetings , time and time again, with promises to fulfill them. Does the board not monitor you for these failures? What is legitimate about your leadership and defaulting on board votes?

> Dear Members of the Board,
>
> As mentioned at the Board of Directors meeting last Friday, I wanted to
> provide an update on two pieces of legislation recently introduced in the
> state legislature that, if enacted, would modify the composition of the
> SANDAG Board of Directors:
>
> *AB 24 (DeMaio)*
> This bill, introduced by Assemblymember Carl DeMaio, proposes modifying
> the SANDAG Board of Directors by removing one of the two County Board of
> Supervisors seats and replacing it with a representative from the San Diego
> County Association of Planning Groups. It would also require the remaining
> County Board representative to be from an unincorporated area of the
> county. The bill has been double-referred to the Assembly Local Government
> Committee and the Assembly Transportation Committee. It currently does not
> have a scheduled hearing date.
>
> *SB 240 (Jones)*
> This bill, introduced by Senate Minority Leader Brian Jones, proposes to
> replace the secondary representative from the County Board of Supervisors
> with a resident from an unincorporated area of the County, as selected by a
> majority of the county’s community planning groups, to serve a 1-year term.
> The bill also eliminates the requirement that one Board of Supervisors
> member be from a substantially incorporated district and the other from an
> unincorporated district. This bill has not yet been referred to a policy
> committee in the Senate.
>
> We will continue to monitor these bills and provide you with updates
> accordingly.
>
> Thank you,
> Mario
>

subject: Loveland Parallel Trail. Other options/ Fish Stocking.
body:
Carlos Quintero,Sweetwater Authority General Manager. 

Hello GM Quintero.

How are you? 
As you know ,what actual lake users wanted and want at Loveland was more access. Both you and Andrew Hayes frequently said there are no limits on the possiblities with the funding. I fail to see how the parallel trail makes any sense. For the path shown The elevattion drop is the same as the existing trail.It requires new brush and tree clearing whereas as switch back stays even in the "user defined " area. It requires maintance the same as the exsting trail, and a trash can, or two.It costs more with the 250K bridge plus 200k "parallel trail" plus maintenance than the $400k bridge.As much as I hate to say it the $400k brige makes more sense. Not ast much sense as a switch back and pipe hard scape but more than the current proposal.
Please consider more practical and cost effective option or go with the big bridge and use the additional 50k to put a pedestrian gate on the east end of the lake.
Alternately,  please find a cost effective crossing at the ravine, I have more ideas,  and stock threadfin shad heavily when weather and other conditions are good for it. .DFW will allow that and these forage fish  are good for birds and other wildlife as well as fish. 
Even with the SDGE easement approved, access from the south side is needed. 
Please call me if you want to talk about any of this or email.

A pedestrian gate here and any forward momentum along the shoreling  at this yellow line  is well within the easement and it's legal to walk on Japatul Road.

Thank you,
Russell Walsh.
619-922-6235
